sp25_mt2_E2.1.title: E2.1 - Sum of Two Periodic Signals
sp25_mt2_E2.1.answer:
**Part (a):** If \(p\) and \(q\) are coprime (\(\gcd(p,q)=1\)), then \(r = pq\)

**Part (b):** \(p = 2k\), \(q = 2\ell\), \(\gcd(k,\ell)=1 \rightarrow r = \text{lcm}(2k,2\ell) = 2k\ell\)

**Part (c):** 
• \(\cos(3\pi/4\cdot n)\) has period 8
• \(\sin(3\pi/5\cdot n)\): \(3\pi/5\cdot q = 2\pi m \rightarrow q = 10m/3 \rightarrow\) smallest \(q = 10\)
• \(r = \text{lcm}(8,10) = 40\)

sp25_mt2_E2.2.title: E2.2 - Signal Fusion in Self-Driving Cars
sp25_mt2_E2.2.answer:
**Part (a):**
• \(\langle a_1,a_2\rangle = (1)(-1) + (1)(1) + 0 = 0 \rightarrow \cos \theta_{12} = 0\) (orthogonal)
• \(\langle a_1,a_3\rangle = 1\), \(\|a_1\|=\|a_3\|=\sqrt{2} \rightarrow \cos \theta_{13} = 1/2\)
• \(\langle a_2,a_3\rangle = -1 \rightarrow \cos \theta_{23} = -1/2\)

**Part (b):** Gram-Schmidt:
• \(q_1 = a_1/\sqrt{2} = [1/\sqrt{2}, 1/\sqrt{2}, 0]^T\)
• \(v_2 = a_2 - \langle a_2,q_1\rangle q_1 = [-1,1,0]^T \rightarrow q_2 = [-1/\sqrt{2}, 1/\sqrt{2}, 0]^T\)
• \(v_3 = a_3 - \langle a_3,q_1\rangle q_1 - \langle a_3,q_2\rangle q_2 = [0,0,1]^T \rightarrow q_3 = [0,0,1]^T\)

sp25_mt2_E2.3.title: E2.3 - Robot Motion in 2D
sp25_mt2_E2.3.answer:
**Part (a):** Rotation then translation (TR):
• \(Rp = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-1\\2\end{bmatrix}\)
• \(T(Rp) = \begin{bmatrix}-1\\2\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}3\\2\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2\\4\end{bmatrix}\)

**Part (b):** Translation then rotation (RT):
• \(Tp = \begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}3\\2\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}5\\3\end{bmatrix}\)
• \(R(Tp) = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -1\\1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-3\\5\end{bmatrix}\)

**Part (c):** \(TR \neq RT\) because matrix multiplication is not commutative

sp25_mt2_E2.4.title: E2.4 - Subspace Properties
sp25_mt2_E2.4.answer:
**Part (a):** Verify orthonormality:
• \(\|\phi_i\|^2 = 1\) for all \(i\) ✓
• \(\langle\phi_1,\phi_2\rangle = \langle\phi_1,\phi_3\rangle = \langle\phi_2,\phi_3\rangle = 0\) ✓

**Part (b):** Decompose \(x = [3,4,12]^T\):
• \(X_1 = \langle x,\phi_1\rangle = (3+4+12)/\sqrt{3} = 19/\sqrt{3}\)
• \(X_2 = \langle x,\phi_2\rangle = (3-12)/\sqrt{2} = -9/\sqrt{2}\)
• \(X_3 = \langle x,\phi_3\rangle = (3-8+12)/\sqrt{6} = 7/\sqrt{6}\)

**Part (c):** By Parseval's theorem: \(\|X\|_2 = \|x\|_2 = \sqrt{9+16+144} = 13\)

sp25_mt2_E2.5.title: E2.5 - Discrete-Time Fourier Series
sp25_mt2_E2.5.answer:
**Part (a):** Period \(p=4\), \(\omega_0=\pi/2\):
• \(X_0 = \frac{1}{4}(2-1-1+2) = \frac{1}{2}\)
• \(X_1 = \frac{1}{4}\sum x[n]e^{-j\pi n/2} = \frac{i\sqrt{3}}{3}\)
• \(X_2 = \frac{1}{4}\sum x[n]e^{-j\pi n} = 0\)
• \(X_3 = X_1^* = \frac{-i\sqrt{3}}{3}\)

**Part (b):** \(x[n] = X_0 + X_1e^{j\pi n/2} + X_3e^{j3\pi n/2} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\sin(\pi n/2)\)
\(\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\beta\) varies depending on form

sp25_mt2_E2.6.title: E2.6 - Matching Null Spaces
sp25_mt2_E2.6.answer:
**Part (a):** \(N(A) \subseteq N(A^TA)\):
• \(x \in N(A) \rightarrow Ax = 0\)
• \(A^TAx = A^T(Ax) = A^T0 = 0 \rightarrow x \in N(A^TA)\) ✓

**Part (b):** \(N(A^TA) \subseteq N(A)\):
• \(x \in N(A^TA) \rightarrow A^TAx = 0\)
• \(x^T(A^TA)x = 0 \rightarrow \|Ax\|^2 = 0\)
• \(\|Ax\| = 0 \rightarrow Ax = 0 \rightarrow x \in N(A)\) ✓

fa24_mt2_MT2.1.title: MT2.1 - Rotation! Rotation! Rotation!
fa24_mt2_MT2.1.answer:
**Part (a):** \(R^{-1} = R^T = \begin{bmatrix}\cos \theta & \sin \theta\\-\sin \theta & \cos \theta\end{bmatrix} = R(-\theta)\)

**Part (b):** \(G_R = R^TR = I\) (orthogonal matrix)

**Part (c):** \(R^n = \begin{bmatrix}\cos(n\theta) & -\sin(n\theta)\\\sin(n\theta) & \cos(n\theta)\end{bmatrix}\)

**Part (d):** \(z(n) = (1/2)^nR(n\pi/2)z(0)\)
• Spirals inward with decay factor 1/2
• \(\lim_{n\to\infty} z(n) = \begin{bmatrix}0\\0\end{bmatrix}\)

fa24_mt2_MT2.2.title: MT2.2 - Triangular Matrices
fa24_mt2_MT2.2.answer:
**Part (a):** Proof using transpose:
• \(L\) lower-triangular invertible \(\iff\) diagonal \(\neq 0\)
• For \(U\): consider \(L = U^T \rightarrow U\) invertible \(\iff\) diagonal \(\neq 0\) ✓

**Part (b):** \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\2&0&0\\3&2&1\end{bmatrix}\):
• \(N(A) = \text{span}\{[0,1,-2]^T\}\)
• \(C(A) = \text{span}\{[1,2,3]^T, [0,0,1]^T\}\)
• \(N(A^T) = \text{span}\{[-2,1,0]^T\}\)
• \(C(A^T) = \text{span}\{[1,0,0]^T, [3,2,1]^T\}\)

**Part (c):** \(B = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\-2/3&1/3&0\\-1/9&-5/18&1/6\end{bmatrix}\)

fa24_mt2_MT2.3.title: MT2.3 - Solving Systems with Singular Matrices
fa24_mt2_MT2.3.answer:
**Part (a):** \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\3&-6\end{bmatrix}\) not invertible:
• \(\text{rank}(A) = 1 < 2\)
• \(\det(A) = -6+6 = 0\)

**Part (b):** \(b = [1,12]^T \rightarrow\) No solution
• \(C(A) = \text{span}\{[1,3]^T\}\)
• \([1,12]^T \neq \alpha[1,3]^T\) for any \(\alpha\)

**Part (c):** \(b = [2,6]^T \rightarrow\) Infinite solutions
• \(b = 2[1,3]^T \in C(A)\) ✓
• \(x_p = [2,0]^T\)
• \(N(A) = \text{span}\{[2,1]^T\}\)
• \(x = [2,0]^T + t[2,1]^T\) for all \(t \in \mathbb{R}\)

fa24_mt2_MT2.5.title: MT2.5 - DTFS
fa24_mt2_MT2.5.answer:
**Part (a)(i):** For odd real signal:
• \(X_{-k} = \frac{1}{p}\sum x(-n)e^{ik\omega_0 n} = -X_k\) ✓

**Part (a)(ii):** For real signal \(X_{-k} = \bar{X}_k\), combined with \(X_{-k} = -X_k\):
• \(\bar{X}_k = -X_k \rightarrow \text{Re}(X_k) = 0 \rightarrow X_k\) purely imaginary ✓

**Part (b)(i):** Period 3, \(\omega_0=2\pi/3\):
• \(X_0 = 0\), \(X_1 = i\sqrt{3}/3\), \(X_2 = -i\sqrt{3}/3\)

**Part (b)(ii):** \(x[n] = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\sin(2\pi n/3)\)
\(\alpha = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\), \(\beta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\)

**Part (b)(iii):** \(\langle X,X\rangle = |X_1|^2 + |X_2|^2 = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\)

sp24_mt2_MT2.1.title: MT2.1 - Permutation Matrices
sp24_mt2_MT2.1.answer:
**Part (a):** \(P^TP = I\) because:
• Diagonal: \((P^TP)_{ii} = 1\) (same position has 1)
• Off-diagonal: \((P^TP)_{ij} = 0\) (different positions)

**Part (b):** \(PAP^T = \begin{bmatrix}0&0&a\\b&c&0\\d&e&0\end{bmatrix}\)

**Part (c)(i):** \(\mu_y = \frac{1}{n}1^TPx = \frac{1}{n}(P^T1)^Tx = \mu_x\) (since \(P^T1=1\))

**Part (c)(ii):** \(\sigma_y^2 = \|Px\|^2/n - \mu_x^2 = \|x\|^2/n - \mu_x^2 = \sigma_x^2\) (\(P\) orthogonal)

**Part (c)(iii):** \(\sigma_{xy} = \frac{1}{n}x^TPx - \mu_x^2\)

sp24_mt2_MT2.2.title: MT2.2 - Correlation Coefficient
sp24_mt2_MT2.2.answer:
**Part (a):** In \(\mathbb{R}^2\), any two vectors are parallel:
• \(\tilde{x} = \frac{x_1-x_2}{2}[1,-1]^T\)
• \(\tilde{y} = \frac{y_1-y_2}{2}[1,-1]^T\)
• \(\rho_{xy} = \pm 1\) depending on signs

**Part (b)(i):** \(\beta \neq 0\) because \(y_1 \neq y_2\)

**Part (b)(ii):** \(\gamma = \mu_y - \beta\mu_x\) (take mean of both sides)

**Part (b)(iii):** \(\tilde{y} = \beta\tilde{x} \rightarrow \rho_{xy} = \beta/|\beta| = \text{sgn}(\beta)\)

**Part (c):** True. Any \(x,y\) in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) with distinct components can be written as affine functions of each other

sp24_mt2_MT2.4.title: MT2.4 - Projection Matrices
sp24_mt2_MT2.4.answer:
**Part (a):** \(P = \frac{aa^T}{a^Ta}\) from orthogonality condition \(\langle a,b-\hat{b}\rangle=0\)

**Part (b):** \(\text{rank}(P) = 1\) (column space is \(\text{span}\{a\}\))

**Part (c)(i):** \(P^T = \frac{(aa^T)^T}{a^Ta} = \frac{aa^T}{a^Ta} = P\) ✓

**Part (c)(ii):** \(P^2 = P\) (idempotent), projecting twice = projecting once

**Part (d):** \(Py = 0 \rightarrow \frac{a(a^Ty)}{a^Ta} = 0 \rightarrow a^Ty = 0 \rightarrow \langle a,y\rangle = 0\)

**Part (e)(i):** \(S^k = S\) for all \(k\geq 1\)

**Part (e)(ii):** If \(Py=0\) then \(Sy = (I-P)y = y\)

**Part (e)(iii):** \(N(S) = \text{span}\{a\}\) (\(Sa = a-Pa = 0\))

**Part (e)(iv):** \(\text{rank}(S) = n-1\)

sp24_mt2_MT2.5.title: MT2.5 - Inner Products with Matrices
sp24_mt2_MT2.5.answer:
**Part (a):** \(W = I\)

**Part (b):** \(W = \begin{bmatrix}0&3\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\) not inner product:
• Not symmetric: \(W^T \neq W\)
• Counter: \(\langle[1,-1]^T,[1,-1]^T\rangle_W = -4 < 0\)

**Part (c):** \(W = \begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\) is inner product:
• Symmetric ✓
• \(x^TWx = 2a^2+2ab+2b^2 = (a-b)^2/2 + 3(a+b)^2/2 \geq 0\) ✓
• \(=0\) only if \(a=b=0\) ✓

**Part (d):** If \(w_{11}=0\), choose \(x=e_1\):
• \(\langle e_1,e_1\rangle_W = w_{11} = 0\) but \(e_1\neq 0\) (violates property 4)

**Part (e):** If \(W\) not invertible, \(\exists v\neq 0: Wv=0\)
• \(\langle v,v\rangle_W = v^TWv = 0\) but \(v\neq 0\) (violates property 4)

sp25_mt3_E3.1.title: E3.1 - Special QR Decomposition in 2D
sp25_mt3_E3.1.answer:
For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}\):
• First column: \(q_1 = [a,c]^T/\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\)
• Orthogonal to \(q_1\): \(q_2 = [-c,a]^T/\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\)
• \(Q = \frac{1}{\sqrt{a^2+c^2}}\begin{bmatrix}a&-c\\c&a\end{bmatrix}\)
• \(R = Q^TA\) (upper triangular)

sp25_mt3_E3.4.title: E3.4 - Basic SVD
sp25_mt3_E3.4.answer:
\(A = \begin{bmatrix}3&2\\1&0\\0&\sqrt{6}\end{bmatrix}\)
• \(A^TA = \begin{bmatrix}10&6\\6&10\end{bmatrix}\)
• Eigenvalues of \(A^TA\): \(\lambda_1=16\), \(\lambda_2=4\)
• Singular values: \(\sigma_1=4\), \(\sigma_2=2\)
• \(V\) from eigenvectors of \(A^TA\)
• \(U\) from \(Av_i/\sigma_i\) or \(AA^T\) eigenvectors
• \(A = U\Sigma V^T\)

sp25_mt3_E3.5.title: E3.5 - Using PCA to Analyze Bacteria
sp25_mt3_E3.5.answer:
PCA steps:
1. Center data: \(\tilde{X} = X - \text{mean}\)
2. Compute covariance: \(C = \tilde{X}\tilde{X}^T/n\)
3. Find eigenvalues/eigenvectors of \(C\)
4. Principal components = eigenvectors with largest eigenvalues
5. Project data onto principal components for classification

fa24_mt3_MT3.1.title: MT3.1 - Hide and Seek
fa24_mt3_MT3.1.answer:
Eigendecomposition: \(T = V\Lambda V^{-1}\)
• \(V = [v_1 \cdots v_n]\) (eigenvectors)
• \(\Lambda = \text{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) (eigenvalues)
• Change of basis: \(x = Cz\) transforms coordinates
• \(T^n = V\Lambda^n V^{-1}\)

fa24_mt3_MT3.2.title: MT3.2 - Ridge Regression
fa24_mt3_MT3.2.answer:
Standard: \(\hat{x} = (A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb\) (may not exist if \(A^TA\) singular)

Ridge: \(\hat{x} = (A^TA + \eta I)^{-1}A^Tb\)
• Eigenvalues: \(\lambda_i(A^TA+\eta I) = \lambda_i(A^TA) + \eta > 0\)
• Always invertible for \(\eta > 0\)

fa24_mt3_MT3.3.title: MT3.3 - Robot Grasping with PCA
fa24_mt3_MT3.3.answer:
PCA for pose estimation:
1. Find center: \((\bar{x},\bar{y}) = \text{mean of points}\)
2. Covariance matrix \(C\)
3. Major axis = eigenvector of largest eigenvalue

State-space: \(x[i+1] = Bx[i] + cu[i]\)
• Solve using SVD for least-norm control \(u^*\)

fa24_mt3_MT3.4.title: MT3.4 - Damped Harmonic Oscillator
fa24_mt3_MT3.4.answer:
\(\ddot{y} = -c\dot{y} - ky \rightarrow\) State-space: \(\frac{dx}{dt} = Ax\)
• \(x = [y,\dot{y}]^T\)
• \(A = \begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-k&-c\end{bmatrix}\)
• Eigenvalues determine stability: \(\text{Re}(\lambda) < 0\) for stability
• Solution: \(x(t) = e^{At}x(0) = Ve^{\Lambda t}V^{-1}x(0)\)

fa23_final_Q4.title: Q4 - Strike a Chord

Inner products and angles:

• Parallel: \(|\cos \theta| = 1\)

fa23_final_Q6.title: Q6 - Let's Go, Mooncow!

fa23_final_Q8.title: Q8 - Aficiona-dough

Markov chain: \(x[k+1] = Px[k]\)

fa23_final_Q9.title: Q9 - Proofs
fa23_final_Q9.answer:
Eigenvector \(v\) of \(A\) with eigenvalue \(\lambda\):
• \(Av = \lambda v\)
• \((A-\lambda I)v = 0\)
• \(v \in N(A-\lambda I)\)

fa23_final_Q10.title: Q10 - Orthonormal Least Squares
fa23_final_Q10.answer:
If \(Q\) has orthonormal columns (\(Q^TQ=I\)):
• Projection: \(P = QQ^T\)
• \(\hat{x} = Q^Tb\) (no matrix inversion needed)
• Residual: \(e = b - QQ^Tb \perp C(Q)\)

sp23_final_Q4.title: Q4 - Least Squares in Pictures
sp23_final_Q4.answer:

• \(A^Te = 0 \rightarrow A^TA\hat{x} = A^Tb\) (normal equations)

sp23_final_Q5.title: Q5 - Battleships
sp23_final_Q5.answer:
Linear regression:
• Formulate: \(Ax = b\) (overdetermined)

• Minimizes: \(\|Ax-b\|^2\)

sp23_final_Q9.title: Q9 - Noisy Imaging Revisited
sp23_final_Q9.answer:
Masking matrix \(M\) (diagonal):
• \(N(M)\) = pixels to remove
• \(C(M)\) = pixels to keep
• Least squares with noise: \(\hat{x} = (A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb\)

sp23_final_Q10.title: Q10 - Charge Pumps
sp23_final_Q10.answer:
State evolution: \(q[n+1] = Pq[n]\)
• Steady state: \((P-I)q_{ss} = 0\) or \(Pq_{ss} = q_{ss}\)
• Convergence rate: second-largest \(|\lambda_2|\)

sp23_final_Q11.title: Q11 - Fun with EECS16(AB)
sp23_final_Q11.answer:

fa22_final_Q3.title: Q3 - Least Squares
fa22_final_Q3.answer:
Standard least squares:

• \(\hat{x} = (A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb\)
• Projection: \(\hat{b} = A\hat{x}\)

fa22_final_Q5.title: Q5 - Eigenstuff
fa22_final_Q5.answer:
Finding eigenvalues/eigenvectors:

2. Solve for \(\lambda\)
3. For each \(\lambda\): solve \((A-\lambda I)v = 0\)
4. Eigenspace = \(N(A-\lambda I)\)

fa22_final_Q10.title: Q10 - Orthogonal Space
fa22_final_Q10.answer:
Orthogonal complement \(V^\perp\):
• \(V^\perp = \{w : \langle v,w\rangle = 0 \text{ for all } v \in V\}\)
• \(\dim(V) + \dim(V^\perp) = n\)
• \(V \cap V^\perp = \{0\}\)

fa22_final_Q11.title: Q11 - Mixed signals?
fa22_final_Q11.answer:
Fit \(y(t) = a \cos(\omega t) + b \sin(\omega t)\):

• Least squares: \(\hat{x} = (A^TA)^{-1}A^Ty\)

sp22_final_Q4.title: Q4 - Eurovision Song Contest
sp22_final_Q4.answer:

sp22_final_Q6.title: Q6 - R-I-P Loads

Power model: \(P = aV^2 + bV + c\)
• \(A = \begin{bmatrix}V_1^2 & V_1 & 1\\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots\end{bmatrix}\)
• Least squares: \([a,b,c]^T = (A^TA)^{-1}A^TP\)

sp22_final_Q7.title: Q7 - Danville Doozy
sp22_final_Q7.answer:
Column-stochastic \(P\) (columns sum to 1):
• Conserves total quantity
• Steady state: \(Px_{ss} = x_{ss}\) (\(\lambda=1\))
• Convergence: \(\rho(P-I) < 1\)

sp22_final_Q12.title: Q12 - Eigenvalues Galore
sp22_final_Q12.answer:
If \(Av = \lambda v\):
• \(A^kv = \lambda^k v\) (eigenvalue of \(A^k\) is \(\lambda^k\))
• \((A+cI)v = \lambda v+cv = (\lambda+c)v\)
• \((cA)v = c(\lambda v) = (c\lambda)v\)

sp21_final_Q3.title: Q3 - Linear Algebra
sp21_final_Q3.answer:

• \(C(A) = \text{span}\{\text{pivot columns}\}\)
• \(N(A)\) from free variables
• \(\text{rank}(A) + \dim(N(A)) = n\)

sp21_final_Q4.title: Q4 - Transitioning Back to Campus
sp21_final_Q4.answer:

• Eigenvalue 1 guarantees convergence

sp21_final_Q9.title: Q9 - Cool Predictions

sp21_final_Q10.title: Q10 - Symmetric and PSD Matrices
sp21_final_Q10.answer:

fa21_final_Q15.title: Q15 - Charge Sharing Cycles
fa21_final_Q15.answer:

hw4_HW4.1.title: HW4.1 - Vector Statistics
hw4_HW4.1.answer:

hw4_HW4.3.title: HW4.3 - Orthogonal Constructions

构造V = {v₁,...,vₙ,-v₁,...,-vₙ}共2n个向量

设v₁...vₙ为Rⁿ的正交基，定义vₙ₊ᵢ = -vᵢ。对于i≠j：
• 若i,j都≤n或都>n：⟨vᵢ,vⱼ⟩ = 0（正交基性质）
• 若j>n, i≤n且i+n≠j：⟨vᵢ,vⱼ⟩ = -⟨vᵢ₊ₙ,vⱼ⟩ = 0
• 若j>n, i≤n且i+n=j：⟨vᵢ,-vᵢ⟩ = -‖vᵢ‖² ≤ 0

因此V span Rⁿ且⟨vᵢ,vⱼ⟩ ≤ 0对所有i≠j成立
